task: Fix the object serialization failure after the library version was upgraded without updating the schema.

candidate_memories.content: Serialization fails with schema mismatch errors after upgrading protobuf from 3.20 to 4.0.
Protobuf 4.0 removed support for the optional keyword at the message level; fields must use explicit optional types.
The proto files use the old optional message syntax that was deprecated in protobuf 3 and removed in 4.
When upgrading protobuf major versions, migrate all proto files before upgrading the runtime library.
Only proto files that use the deprecated optional keyword are affected; required and repeated fields serialize correctly.
The project uses protobuf for inter-service communication and for storage serialization.
Session 5 note: the platform team added proto file linting to the CI pipeline.
Old lesson: the optional keyword was added for backward compatibility with proto2 files.
Proto files are compiled during the build and the generated code is committed to the repository.
Session 10 note: the data team migrated 12 proto files from proto2 to proto3 syntax.
Old proto guide: optional was the recommended field modifier for nullable fields in proto3.
Major version upgrades to serialization libraries must be preceded by a full proto file audit.
Session 7 note: the API team added a proto file for the new notification service.
The gRPC framework is used for all inter-service calls; REST is only used for external client-facing APIs.
A compatibility test in session 3 verified that old clients can read messages from new services.
Proto file changes require a backward compatibility review before they can be merged.
Serialization format changes must be dual-written during migration to prevent data loss.
Session 12 note: the monitoring team added a serialization error rate metric to the dashboard.
Old gRPC guide: proto3 was adopted to simplify service contracts and remove required field constraints.
The schema registry stores the canonical proto file versions for all services.
